compiled_state.title: As an operator, running /debug-everything with merge.strategy=pr opens a long-lived aggregate draft PR and creates a .debug-active marker; running with merge.strategy=direct preserves current behavior
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Add /debug-everything Phase B Step 1 ci-pr-mode initialization that reads `merge.strategy`, opens a long-lived aggregate draft PR via parameterized `create-sprint-draft-pr.sh` (DRAFT_PR_TITLE_PREFIX=Debug:), creates a `.debug-active` marker, emits a startup log, with Phase A stale-marker cleanup and Phase K marker removal. Document the `.debug-active` marker as a normative shared schema.

**Why**: Activates the ci-pr workflow gated on existing `merge.strategy=pr` config (no new key per design); preserves backward compatibility when set to `direct` or unset.

**Scope**:
- IN: Read `merge.strategy` at Phase B Step 1; when `pr`, open aggregate draft PR + create `.debug-active` marker with `debug-session-id` format `<UTC-timestamp>-<6-char-random>` (e.g., `20260512-141045-a3f9c2`) + schema_version field; emit one-line resolved-mode startup log; Phase A entry cleans stale `.debug-active` markers (session-id not in live process table OR embedded timestamp older than configurable TTL, default 24h); Phase A pre-upgrade safety: refuse ci-pr operations against a marker pattern indicating a pre-upgrade in-flight session until explicit restart; Phase K removes marker; document marker schema in skill docs and reference from S2/S10.
- OUT: Sub-branch creation logic (S4/S5); review wiring (S6); leak detection (S9); DEBUG_BRANCH_TRACKING comments (S7).

## Done Definitions

- When complete, /debug-everything started with `merge.strategy=pr` opens a long-lived aggregate draft PR via the parameterized `create-sprint-draft-pr.sh` with `DRAFT_PR_TITLE_PREFIX=Debug:` and creates a `.debug-active` marker
  ← Satisfies: "When /debug-everything runs with merge.strategy=pr, Phase B Step 1 opens a long-lived aggregate draft PR"
- When complete, the `.debug-active` marker contains a `debug-session-id` of format `<UTC-timestamp>-<6-char-random>` and a `schema_version` field, documented as a normative shared schema readable by S2's hook and S10's PreToolUse hook
  ← Satisfies: "Phase B Step 1 creates a .debug-active marker containing the resolved debug-session-id"
- When complete, Phase A entry treats a `.debug-active` marker as stale and removes it when (a) the embedded session-id has no matching live process OR (b) the embedded timestamp is older than the configurable TTL (default 24h); pre-upgrade in-flight pattern detection refuses ci-pr until explicit restart
  ← Satisfies: "Phase A entry detects and removes stale .debug-active markers"
- When complete, running /debug-everything with `merge.strategy=direct` (or absent) creates no `.debug-active` marker, no aggregate draft PR, and emits a startup log line `merge.strategy=direct — debug session running in local mode`
  ← Satisfies: "merge.strategy=direct (or absent) preserves current behavior end-to-end"
- When complete, Phase K removes the `.debug-active` marker before /debug-everything exits
  ← Satisfies: "Marker is removed at Phase K"
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
  ← Satisfies: "Phase B Step 1 creates a .debug-active marker"

## Considerations

- [Reliability] Pre-upgrade in-flight session detection is a corner case worth a dedicated test; TTL fallback (24h) handles SIGKILL + PID-reuse cases
- [Maintainability] The `.debug-active` marker is read by S2's hook and S10's PreToolUse hook — schema must be specified once here and referenced from both consumers

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
